podcast.body: The band's self-titled debut album, featuring David Bowie on vocals, was filled with noisy rock and billed as Bowie's return to his roots as a small rock combo frontman. Its metallic, feedback-laden sound was influenced by art punk bands like Pixies and Sonic Youth. The album reached number 28 and did not go gold, struggling to gain an identity beyond Bowie's side project. "He released a self-titled album filled with noisy rock."

podcast.body: This self-titled album was the debut record of the four-piece rock band formed by David Bowie, who served solely as the lead singer. The band's sound was a deliberate departure from Bowie's previous solo work, inspired by artists like Jimi Hendrix, Cream, and the Pixies. Released between 1989 and 1991, the album and its follow-up received harsh reviews, with some critics perceiving Bowie as attempting to regain relevance. "Tin Machine from their self-titled Davy album and a single entitled Under the God."
